metadata.summary: First Samuel 17 narrates David's defeat of Goliath during an Israelite-Philistine standoff, emphasizing contrasting weapons, public speech, contested kingship, and confidence in YHWH rather than military stature.

evidence_items.claim: The David and Goliath account exists in a substantially shorter ancient Greek form and a longer Masoretic form; reconstruction of their literary relationship remains disputed.

Excavated workshop features and metallurgical residues at Tell es-Safi/Gath document iron and bronze production in Iron Age IIA Philistia.

The workshop makes Philistine metal production materially plausible within the wider Iron Age setting and helps readers understand why Samuel can foreground weapon materials, while it does not authenticate Goliath's equipment or prove exclusive Philistine technology.
